title: My game dev inspiration, good old 90's gaming.
author: CoolTIOnline
selftext:
You guys will have to excuse the cringe... My skill is in support and network administration, not in making marketing videos.If you aren't interested in my retro gaming introduction, the gameplay of my game starts at 5:00.

What's in my game right now:

\-A basic campaign with X amount of maps to beat per level.  
\-Up to 4 players local split screen  
\-Online or LAN multiplayer up to 8 players, teams from 1v1 to 4v4, FFA or Team FFA with voice chatradio channel system concept.  
\-Built-in map editor  
\-Two game modes: Capture the Flag or Destroy the enemy base.  
\-Tanks, APC, Rocket Tank, Jeeps and Helicopters, each with their own handling and sounds.  
\-AI players that fill empty seats, plus soldiers, smaller tanks, attack helicopters and defense towers that can be assigned as player assets for defense or environment which attacks everyone.  
\-Minimap with fog of war  
\-Arcade car handling for FWD, RWD and AWD cars. Added the handbreak of course because who doesn't like to do handbrake turns.  
\-If someone is knocked out in a team multiplayer game, he can grab one of the city cars and joyride around the map lobbing grenades at other players. (Though you are a fun and easy target)  
\-In-game manual

I always dreamed of making a videogame but coding has never been my thing. I simply suck at languages.  
Back when I was 17 I went into computer science and I just hated C++. I later went into I.T. Networking, worked and grew in the field ever since.

With that being said,

I am no coding expert so my game wouldn't exist if Claude wasn't here to help me realize my vision.  
The music is a mix of licensed classical tracks such as The Hall Of Mountain King, Flight Of The Valkyries, and some others generated with Suno.

I have also used Tripo to generate 3D models to then fix and correct them using Blender.

Regardless of the use of AI, I have been working hard on this for some time and happy to say I learned so much about coding, game design and blender.

It was fun learning Godot, making a 2D concept, then switching to 3D and leaning none stop as I go. Initially I never thought I would get this far.

I am always open for any feedback on the game, questions or suggestions.

Built with Godot. More info and the dev logs: [www.retaliationrun.com](http://www.retaliationrun.com)  
More gameplay videos: [https://www.youtube.com/@RetaliationRun](https://www.youtube.com/@RetaliationRun)

I messed up my Steamworks initial request. I mistyped some information so I had to restart the process from scratch. As 30 Business days is a long time, I exported a free Demo of my game and uploaded it to [Itch.io](http://Itch.io)

[https://retaliationrun.itch.io/demo](https://retaliationrun.itch.io/demo)

The following is available in the demo.

* Campaign levels 1 to 4
* 1v1 online multiplayer
* Online Score and Ranking
* Split screen
* (The map maker is only in the full game.)

I plan on adding more content and if the demand is there, I will update and upload a newer version with 4 player multiplayer.

As a 43 year old married guy with a full time job, all my friends are married with kids... so I tested as much as I can and I would be grateful for any feedback.

Cheers.

comments.author: InvertedVantage
comments.body: I'll download the game - I've been trying to find the name of Return Fire for AGES! Used to love playing that game.

replies.author: CoolTIOnline
replies.body:
Awesome!   
Please let me know what you think. Also let me know when you will give it a shot, I would love to test the multiplayer more.

replies.author: CoolTIOnline
replies.body:
Cool. Thanks for the feedback!

1- The text I added as how to play instructions, there is a checkmark on the first text to disable it. I will look into making the "Don't show me instructions" option to be more noticeable.

2- I will look into adding the screen relative controls. Though I am pretty sure that's how they are even in the classic Return Fire game. I will have to double check.

3- I forgot about that. It's something I added in an early build and completely forgot to remove it. I never liked it and shy's away from the original.

4- There is a dink but also a number of other sound effects. Also there are sparks or explosions for rockets. I will look into improving the hit sounds and review the hit effects and see if I can improve on that.

5- Noted. I will review the bridge sides and make sure the fix the shooting collisions over the bridges.

6- UX? I tried to fight this by adding some form of screen movement in the direction the weapons are pointing. Mostly for pointing down given the games light angle, that way when going down, we have the same view distance as going up.  
I think that when looking at corners, the zoom takes even more place to the sides?

I am hosting a game to, it should pop up automatically if you want to give it a shot.  
Edit: I waited a bit but sadly I need to go out meet up with a friend.  
Cheers and thanks again for the first impression. Ill work on that and upload a revision asap.
